tasks.name: Saturday Morning
tasks.text: On Saturday morning Dad wakes Ollie early: Get up, my assistant! Today we go to the market. Ollie likes this tradition. They take two big bags and go out. On the way they meet Mr. Carter and George. George has never seen a real market — in London he went to the supermarket. Today he will see a very different place! At the entrance there are flowers, berries and a lot of people. The smell of fresh bread and herbs is everywhere. Come on, our seller is waiting!

tasks.name: At Mr. Fisher's
tasks.text: Mr. Fisher is already waiting at his stall. Good morning, David! Good morning, little captain! he says to Ollie. Today he has wonderful fish: herring, cod and salmon. Dad chooses a big fish for dinner. Mr. Fisher asks: And who is this young man? George answers: I am George, a friend from England. Mr. Fisher laughs: England! Welcome to our market! Dad pays, and Mr. Fisher gives the boys each an apple. This market is the friendliest in the city!

tasks.name: Vegetables and Fruit
tasks.text: Then they go to the next stalls. Mum's list is long: potatoes, tomatoes, carrots, cucumbers and onions. Dad takes grapes and plums. Ollie sees a stall with honey and asks: Can we buy honey for tea? Dad nods: One jar. Mr. Carter buys cheese and fresh milk. George looks at everything and says: Here you can see, smell and choose everything. In the supermarket, everything is in boxes! Ollie teaches him: We say kilo and half a kilo — this is the market language of numbers.

tasks.name: How Much Does It Cost?
tasks.text: At one stall Ollie sees beautiful berries. How much does it cost? he asks. The seller answers: Ten coins for one box. Ollie counts his money: one, two, three... ten! He carefully gives the coins and takes the box — a surprise for Mum. Then Dad shows him other money: This coin is one, this note is ten, and this note is fifty. Money likes to be counted, Dad smiles. Ollie agrees: Now I know it! Shopping is a real school of numbers.

tasks.name: Back Home
tasks.text: The bags are heavy, but the way home is happy. George helps and carries a bag of potatoes. On the road the boys talk about food: what is tastier — fish or pizza? George says: Fish, of course! At home Mum opens the bags: Fresh vegetables, fish and honey! And here is my surprise — berries! Ollie says proudly: I bought them myself. Mum hugs him: Thank you, my dear! In the evening the family eats soup with fresh vegetables, and George tells his parents: Your market is the best!

tasks.name: The Shopping List
tasks.text: In the evening Dad looks into the fridge and says: We have nothing for dinner! Mum takes a paper and writes a shopping list. Everyone adds something: Mum — milk and cheese, Jack — pasta, Sophie — fruit and yoghurt, and Ollie — bread and chocolate, for a good mood. Then Bella lies down right on the list. Buddy looks at the paper and wants to eat it. Dad saves the list just in time: Shopping with this family is not easy! Tomorrow we will buy everything.

tasks.name: Carts and Shelves
tasks.text: On Tuesday the family goes to the supermarket together. Ollie takes a big cart and rides it like a car. The supermarket has many shelves: drinks, meat, fish, dairy, bread and vegetables. Sophie reads the names and helps Mum: Milk is here, in the dairy part. Jack looks at pasta and chooses the longest one. Ollie wants to put chips in the cart, but Mum says: No chips today, we have a list. Then she gives him another job: Find six eggs. Ollie finds them quickly and is very proud. The cart is almost full.

tasks.name: At the Checkout
tasks.text: At the checkout there is a little queue. The cashier scans the food: milk, cheese, pasta, bread, eggs, fruit, chocolate... and the prices on the screen grow and grow. Dad pays with a card. Then he gets a long receipt. Ollie looks at it: So many numbers! Sophie checks the receipt: Everything is correct. Buddy and Bella at home feel it: something tasty is coming! The cashier smiles: Have a nice day! Dad takes the bags, and the family goes home. On the way Ollie says: Shopping is like a sport!

tasks.name: Packing at Home
tasks.text: At home everyone unpacks the bags together. Mum puts the milk, cheese and yoghurt in the fridge: These are cold things. Sophie puts the pasta and bread in the kitchen cabinet — these are dry things. Jack washes the tomatoes and cucumbers, and Ollie looks for the chocolate... He finds it and asks: Can I eat one piece? Just one, says Mum. The bags become empty, and the kitchen becomes full. Dad says: Now we have food for a week! Then the family drinks tea with chocolate. Even Buddy gets a little piece — if he sits nicely!

tasks.name: Dinner from the List
tasks.text: In the evening the family cooks dinner from the shopping list. Jack makes pasta with cheese and tomatoes — it is his day. Sophie cuts fruit for a salad. Ollie sets the table and puts the bread in a basket. Mum helps and laughs: Now you are a real team of cooks! Dad tastes the pasta: Delicious! Jack is proud: It is my favourite recipe. Then everyone eats and talks about the day. The best dinners are the ones you make from a simple list.

tasks.name: The Invitation
tasks.text: Mr. Carter comes down and says: I love pelmeni! Can you teach us to cook them? Mum laughs: With pleasure! On Saturday at eleven o'clock the Carters come with flour and meat. Mum gives everyone an apron. Emily gets the smallest apron and a little rolling pin. George asks: Is it difficult? Mum answers: No, but it needs many hands. The kitchen becomes noisy and funny. Mr. Carter writes new words in his notebook: flour, dough, to roll, filling. He says: Pelmeni are my favourite Russian lesson — after words, of course!

tasks.name: Dough and Filling
tasks.text: First the dough. Mum puts flour, water, one egg and salt in a big bowl. Emily mixes with a spoon, and George mixes with his hands — now his hands are white. Then the filling: meat, onion and a little pepper. Dad makes the filling and jokes: The main secret is not to cry from the onion! Everyone laughs. Sophie rolls the dough out into a big thin circle. Jack cuts it into small circles. Mr. Carter tries too, but his circles are not round. Nobody cares — taste is more important than form.

tasks.name: Many Hands
tasks.text: Now the most interesting part: everyone makes pelmeni. Mum shows how to do it: a circle of dough, a little filling in the middle, then the edges together — and here is a little hat! Sophie makes big and small pelmeni. Emily is very careful: her pelmeni are small and neat. George makes one huge pelmeni — he says it is for Dad. Ollie makes funny forms: a star, a heart and even a fish. Mr. Carter counts: One, two, three... fifty! Fifty pelmeni and eight hands. And one white nose — Emily's!

tasks.name: Dinner!
tasks.text: Mum cooks the pelmeni in a big pot of hot water. Everyone waits at the table. First the pelmeni swim like little boats, then they come up — that means they are ready! Mum puts them on plates with butter and herbs. Mr. Carter closes his eyes and tastes the first pelmeni: This is happiness! he says. Emily eats six pelmeni! George wants more. Grandma's recipe works again, smiles Mum. For dessert there is tea with jam. Food made together is always the most delicious.

tasks.name: A New Tradition
tasks.text: After dinner Mrs. Carter writes the recipe in her notebook with three stars: Very tasty! George sums up: Dough, filling, many hands, hot water. Now we can cook pelmeni at home. Mrs. Carter says: And next time we will teach you our favourite dish — the English pie with apples and cinnamon. Ollie jumps: I love pies! The parents smile: So every month we will cook together, one new dish. Dough and friendship grow when many hands make them, says Mr. Carter. Everyone agrees.

tasks.name: Peter the Cook
tasks.text: Our neighbour Peter is a chef. He works in a small café near the park. On Friday he invites the whole family: Come to my café, I have a new menu! In the evening the family comes, and the Carters are already there. The café is warm and smells of cake. Peter meets them in a white chef jacket. Ollie asks: Do you cook everything yourself? Yes, and I am proud of my soup! Peter smiles. Then a friendly waiter brings the menus. Dinner will be delicious!

tasks.name: The Menu
tasks.text: The menu is like a small book. First there are starters: vegetable salad and soup. Then the main dishes: fish with potatoes, pasta with cheese and Peter's special pizza. For dessert: ice cream, apple pie and chocolate cake. The children read the menu together. Emily chooses soup and fish. George wants pizza. Ollie cannot choose between ice cream and cake — so he says: Both, please! Mum looks at him: Ollie! He thinks and says: OK, ice cream first, then cake. Everyone laughs: That is a real decision!

tasks.name: The Order
tasks.text: The waiter comes and asks: Are you ready to order? Mr. Carter says politely: I would like the soup and fish, please. Mrs. Carter: And a salad for me, please. The children order pizza and lemonade. Ollie learns a polite phrase: I would like... — it works like a magic key, says Dad. The waiter smiles: Good choice! While they wait, Peter brings warm bread and butter. Emily tries her soup: Delicious! Ollie says Thank you! — and the waiter answers: You are welcome!

tasks.name: Peter's Surprise
tasks.text: After dinner Peter comes to the table with a big plate: This is my surprise for the children! On the plate there are little cakes in the form of a football, a paintbrush and a book — for Ollie, Sophie and Jack. The children shout: Wow! For Mum there is a cake-doctor with a stethoscope, and for Dad a cake-house with a red roof. Everyone is surprised: You are not a cook, you are an artist! Peter laughs: A cook is always a little bit an artist. Then he brings tea for the grown-ups and cocoa for the children.

tasks.name: The Bill
tasks.text: It is late. Dad asks the waiter: The bill, please. The waiter brings a small paper. Dad looks at it and pays. Mum says: Thank you, Peter! It was a wonderful evening! Peter answers: Come again — next time I will make fish soup. George says to Ollie: This is the best café in the city! Ollie agrees: And the best cook in the city! On the way home the family talks about the evening. Dad says: Today we learned an important phrase — I would like... Use it politely, and the world becomes friendlier.
